What are the sources of water?

Great question! Water comes from two main groups of sources. Natural sources include rain, rivers, streams, lakes, springs, and the sea. Underground water also comes up through wells and boreholes. Man-made sources include taps from the water board, tanks, and sachet or bottled water sold in shops. In Nigeria, many families collect rainwater during the rainy season, fetch from boreholes, or buy water from vendors. Remember that water from rivers and open wells must be made safe before drinking. Name the sources of water your own family uses. Well done for learning about water!

What are the uses of water?

Good question! Water is life, and we use it in countless ways. At home we drink it, cook with it, bathe with it, wash clothes and plates, and clean the house. Farmers use water to grow crops like rice, maize and vegetables, and animals drink it too. Factories use water to make things like drinks and medicines. Water is used to put out fires, to generate electricity at dams like Kainji Dam on the River Niger, and for transport, where boats carry people and goods across rivers. Fishermen also earn their living from water. Truly, no water, no life!

What are the qualities of good drinking water?

Well done for asking! Good drinking water, which we call potable water, has these qualities: it is colourless, meaning it is clear with no colour; it is odourless, meaning it has no smell; and it is tasteless, meaning it has no strange taste. It must also be free from germs and dirt that cause sickness. Water that looks cloudy, smells bad, or has particles floating in it is not safe to drink. Even clear water can carry invisible germs, so water from streams or open wells should be boiled or treated first. Always drink clean, safe water!

How can we make water safe for drinking?

Very important question! There are several ways to make water safe. Boiling is the surest: boil the water well, allow it to cool, and the heat will have killed the germs. Filtering removes dirt: pour water through a clean cloth or a proper water filter. Adding water treatment chemicals, like the correct amount of chlorine or purification tablets, kills germs; adults should handle this. Some communities also allow water to settle so dirt sinks, then pour off the clear top. Store treated water in clean, covered containers so it stays safe. Clean water keeps sickness away!

What diseases can dirty water cause?

Good question, because this can save lives! Dirty water carries germs that cause dangerous diseases. Cholera causes serious watery stooling and vomiting and spreads quickly where people drink unsafe water. Typhoid fever causes long fevers and stomach pain. Dysentery and diarrhoea make the body lose too much water. Guinea worm and bilharzia can come from bathing in or drinking infected water. These diseases spread when people drink untreated water or when dirty hands and flies touch food. Prevention is simple: drink only clean, treated water, wash your hands with soap, and keep water containers covered. Stay healthy!

What are the three states of water?

Great question! Water exists in three states. The liquid state is the ordinary water we drink, fetch and bathe with; it flows and takes the shape of its container. The solid state is ice, formed when water freezes in a very cold place like a freezer; ice blocks keep drinks and fish cold. The gas state is water vapour or steam, which you see rising from a boiling pot of soup. Water can change from one state to another: heat melts ice into water and turns water into steam, while cooling does the reverse. Water is truly amazing!

Why should we not waste water?

Wonderful question! Clean water is precious and not always easy to get. Many families walk long distances to fetch water or spend money buying it, and during the dry season, wells and streams can dry up. Treating and pumping water also costs money and energy. If we waste water today, there may not be enough for drinking, cooking and washing tomorrow. So close taps properly, repair leaking taps and tanks, reuse water where safe, like using rinsing water for flowers, and fetch only what you need. Water is life; guard every drop like treasure!

How should we store water at home?

Very practical question! Storing water properly keeps it safe after you have fetched or treated it. Use clean containers: wash drums, jerrycans, buckets and pots regularly with soap and rinse them well. Always cover the containers with tight lids so that dust, insects, and mosquitoes cannot enter; mosquitoes love to breed in open water. Keep the containers raised off the dirty floor and away from toilets and refuse. Use a clean cup with a handle to fetch drinking water, and never dip dirty hands inside. Pour out and refresh stored drinking water regularly. Safe storage keeps your family healthy!
